utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. The affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, Mrs. Jusufi, still applies. Now, Mr. Apostolski, I believe you have still some questions to finish. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. I would like to continue with a few more questions, and I would comprise four topics with them. Cross-examination by Mr. Apostolski (Continued):

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you all the time besides your son after he was injured?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it needs to become a little more clear, Mr. Apostolski, if you would like Ms. Jusufi to answer.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters couldn't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You were asked whether you were with your son all the time after he was injured until he died.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the others, beside him, from the moment of his injury until his death?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Myself, my husband and the -- the uncle's son, Muzafer.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to speak closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated yesterday that when your son was injured, you fainted. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I fainted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you regained consciousness, you saw that your son was bleeding heavily; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have stated that after 15 to 20 minutes after his injury, your son died when you were trying to bandage his wound. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took a sheet to tie his wound, but then he died. He died very soon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whether within this period between the injury and his death, you called someone?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Who should I call? I didn't have a telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has your husband called someone?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we didn't have a telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it mean that your husband never called anyone?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't, because as I said, we did not have a phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has your son phoned someone?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He died. He died after a short while. He couldn't have called anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that at the moment of the injury, in the house there were you, Muzafer and your husband, Elmaz; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has your son spoken with someone else, apart from the three of you, inside the house?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It means that he was not able to talk because his wound was heavy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your son was not able to phone anyone on the phone?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name Fatmir Ademi?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me recall you. He's an MP in the Assembly of the Republic of Macedonia, and he safeguards the interests of the Albanians in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think that he would state anything incorrect regarding the Ljuboten case, considering that he's an MP?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Without having to hear you, Ms. Motoike, that's really not a question anybody can answer, Mr. Apostolski. You might ask whether you would accept my word because I'm a judge. I think you see the point. So you needn't bother to answer that, Mrs. Jusufi. Carry on, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to move for a closed session for a moment, since I will read from a statement of a witness that might be heard before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since they were his cousins, they had very good relations with Rami and had contacts with him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything about that. I know that it's his brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we now move to a closed session, since there is a statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now read from the statement of the witness Xhevdet Jusufovski.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have stated that on the evening after the event, you have left the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have stated that after approximately three weeks, you returned to the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have stated that your house was damaged; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It was riddled with bullets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it for the first time that you cleaned your house from the bullets?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I don't know. When we came back. I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you dispose of the ammunition, and when -- where did you dispose of the ammunition and when?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when we disposed of it and where. The garbage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a bathroom in your house?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated yesterday that you didn't have any running water in your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, we didn't have running water. We had -- but we did have water outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have the Macedonian security forces entered the house?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not inside the house. They came to the gate, the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were injured by some of the security forces?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear your question. No, I wasn't. I was inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has anyone from the security forces spoken to you?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go out. I stayed inside the house. I hid in a corner. Elmaz, that is my husband, knows.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. In line 4 -- 14 -- in line 4, "But you were injured by some of the security forces," it should be "Were you injured by some of the security forces?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated yesterday when your son died in the house, there were only you, your husband and Muzafer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. But you are asking me again and again for the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until the darkness fell. Until darkness fell, nobody came to your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody came, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have stated that when darkness fell, your neighbours and relatives came and moved the body of your son into your daughter's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came and took his body at 2.00 in the morning. Maybe it was 1.00. I don't know, because it was dark. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you could agree with me that this occurred at 2.00 after midnight; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't look at the clock, because I didn't have electricity. It was only dark, it was very dark, so I can't give you a precise time. And I didn't even have the -- it didn't even occur to me to look at the clock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I regret, but I must show to you once again the photograph of your deceased son at the moment of his death, so I would like to ask the usher to show the picture 65 ter 608, ERN 0501-6263.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that tab 1, Exhibit P4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's my son.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This photograph was taken -- this photograph was taken at the moment after the death of your son; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The photograph was taken inside your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember. My husband knows better. I think he was photographed the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this photograph taken by your husband or not, or was it taken by you?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was taken by the hodxa, the Muslim priest, on the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that this photograph was taken inside your daughter's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZENEP JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you now -- that's all, Your Honour. I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Motoike, are there any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Jusufi, you'll be very pleased to know that that is the end of the questions for you. We want to thank you for your assistance. We know it's a very hard time for you. We want to thank you for your trouble in coming to The Hague. And the Court Officer will now take you out of the courtroom. So thank you indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has shown the witness to document 65 ter number 1D1, that was her statement of 3rd of October, 2004, and 65 ter number 1D4, the addition to the statement of Mrs. Jusufi of 22nd of April, 2007. Your Honour, the Defence moves that just for the purposes of discreditation of this witness, these documents are accepted as evidence of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may be heard briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: My understanding is that the normal practice at this Tribunal is that the record is perhaps complete once the witness has testified, and on cross-examination is then confronted with the inconsistencies in any written statements given by the witness, and then that -- those inconsistencies then are recorded into the proceedings for the trial, and so then admission of the statements that the Defence at this time wishes to seek to admit would perhaps clutter the record when the inconsistencies that have already been addressed have been read into the record and addressed by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Anything to submit concerning that, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the jurisprudence of this Tribunal testifies about numerous cases where despite the fact that the witness was shown some contradictions in their statements, the Court would admit, for the purpose of discrediting the witness, also their previous statements. At this moment, I could not indicate all the other cases, but I have had many such cases in the cases of Celebic and Hasan Ricen [phoen] Kubura. I could not quote now all the remaining jurisprudence in this area, so we would like to stay with the motion that we have made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The normal position under the jurisprudence of the Tribunal is that which has been indicated by Ms. Motoike. There are situations where, as a typical example, the extent of the differences between the oral evidence and the previous statement is so considerable or where the context of the full previous statement is important to appreciate the difference, that it becomes of value to actually receive the statement as an exhibit after it has been cross-examined on. But in the Chamber's view, this is not such a case. Ms. Residovic was careful to put to the witness very distinctly each of the material points of difference between a previous statement and the present oral testimony of the witness, so that the record very adequately identifies all the material differences between the oral evidence here and the previous statements of the witness. So we would not receive those previous statements as an exhibit. The next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls Mr. Elmaz Jusufi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: -- who will be testifying pursuant to Rule 92 ter. Your Honour, while we're waiting for the witness, perhaps to speed things up a little bit, I might seek the assistance of one of my learned colleagues. We have brought some hard copies of the -- of the exhibits that will be shown to this witness, because as good, nervous lawyers that we are, we were afraid that the e-court system would not function 100 per cent. So they had been prepared over the weekend. And we also brought some copies of the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jusufi. Do you swear that the evidence you will give will be the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, with your leave, I would like to greet all of you before we begin. Good afternoon, Your Honours of the Hague Tribunal. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. And thank you for giving me the opportunity to come here and testify before this Tribunal. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, indeed. Now, Mr. Saxon has some questions first for you. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I could impose for a moment more on the goodwill of our usher, first of all we have some copies of the exhibits which I intend to show to the witness today, and perhaps if these could be distributed to the Judges, we'd be grateful. And if perhaps a copy -- and we also have some copies of the consolidated 92 ter statement that was produced for this witness, as well as a copy of a document titled "Addenda and Corrections" to that statement. And I'd like, if possible, could a copy of these two documents be placed on the table in front of the witness, so that he can see it easily. And if the Judges would like hard copies as well, we can provide them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is your name Elmaz Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, Elmaz Jusufov.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is the -- is your name -- is your surname, in the Albanian language, "Jusufi"?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: In the Albanian language, it is "Jusufi," and in the Macedonian, "Jusufov."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And are you the husband of Mrs. Zenep Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is your ethnicity Albanian?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you live in the village of Ljuboten in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like you to please focus on a day in April of this year, just two or three weeks ago, when some members of the office that I work for came to your village and spoke to you.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall that those people --

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jusufi, just listen to my questions, please, and focus on them and answer them, and then, please, I will ask the next question. All right? In the past, you had given a couple of statements to members of my office; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in April of this year, you signed another statement that contained parts of those earlier statements; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm wondering perhaps if the usher could place a copy of this statement on the ELMO. English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, could you please -- I'm wondering if the person in the audio-visual booth could pull back a little bit, please, so that we can see the signature at the bottom. Thank you. Mr. Jusufi, is that your signature at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you sign every page of this document?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the last page, please. I'm sorry, Mr. Usher. Can we turn to the page before that? There's a paragraph on that last page that has the title in English "Witness Acknowledgment." Is that your signature on that page?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher, if you could remove that statement from the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, after you signed that statement, did you then make some additions or -- let me start again. Did you then make some changes to that statement?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, there were some changes, minor changes I would say. I made these minor corrections, but they were not that important as far as the context was concerned. Whether it was this date or that date or whether it was the left hand or right hand, these kinds of mistakes, minor mistakes. I would say the majority of the statement was correct:

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I need to impose on your goodwill one more time. There is an additional document that I believe is in front of the witness. If that could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, is that your signature at the bottom of that document?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, can we turn the page, please? And for the person who's working in the audio-visual booth, I need to see what's written at the very top of this page. No, that is the wrong document, sir. We've already seen that document. We need to see a document that has the title, "Additions or Corrections."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you look at the signature on the first page, Mr. Jusufi, again, please, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we turn to the next page, please. And can the camera be moved so that we can see the top of this page, please. And at the top of the page, it says, "Additions or Corrections to the Rule 92 ter Statement by Elmaz Jusufi." Mr. Jusufi, did you sign every page of this document?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, every page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And were the contents of this document read to you in your language before you signed?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the -- can we turn to page 6, please? Mr. Jusufi, is that your signature at the bottom of that page?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, together, would these two documents that you signed in April of this year, represent what you would say today if you were testifying orally?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would seek to tender the consolidated rule 92 ter statement of Mr. Jusufi and the document entitled, "Addenda and Corrections" to the Rule 92 ter statement of Mr. Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we leave that perhaps until after the evidence of this witness so as not to interrupt the flow of his evidence. We'll have some response to the offer made by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well on this occasion, yes, Mr. Mettraux, although the normal process would be to do it at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would be happy to do it now, if you want, Your Honour. The objection which we would have is essentially the one which we raised yesterday. There is a number of concerns as to the manner and way in which the consolidation has taken place. We've sent an e-mail to Mr. Saxon two days ago. He hasn't been able yet to respond to us. But what we would propose to do, is we've asked the Prosecution to provide us with a document which allows us to identify the changes and amendments made, and if they are all agreeable to us, there would be no need for the Chamber to decide anything. I think we could agree with the Prosecution as to whether some of the amendments made are proper and adequate in the circumstances, and we only need the assistance of the Court if the party can't agree that the consolidation is indeed within the realm of Your Honour's order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, in the circumstances, the practical course is for the Chamber to receive both the statement and the document of amendments, and we will take into account any concerns that are pursued in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So if the registry officer could give an exhibit number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document bearing ERN number N006-4132 becomes Exhibit P8. The second document bearing ERN number N006-4121 will become Exhibit P9. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm just collecting in my mind whether it is going to be better in the long run if we have the amendments with the same exhibit number as the main statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe it would be, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It might be less confusing. As we're finding our way, perhaps the Court Officer would be kind enough to re-number the second document as part of Exhibit P8. 8.1 and 8.2 will become the two exhibits. I think it will be easier for everybody then to find the statement and then the amendment later. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, I need to show you a photograph now, and I'm wondering if we could show on the computer screens, from Rule 65 ter number 608, a photograph with ERN 0501-6264, which is tab 1 of the exhibits that have been distributed today. Just for the record, Mr. Jusufi, do you recognise the person in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Of course I do. A man recognises his own child in whatever state he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What was your son's name who is in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Rami Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. If that photograph could be tendered as an exhibit, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P9, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If that photograph could be removed from the screen, please, and if we could show the witness, from Rule 65 ter number 170, a photograph with an ERN N000-7850. This would be tab 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, who is shown in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Elmaz Jusufi, the person you see sitting right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in that photograph, where are you?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: In the corridor. We call it "hodnik," which in English is "corridor."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the corridor of what building, what place?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Of Elmaz Jusufi's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's your home; right?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you appear to be sitting very close to a door.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. The door to the room is opposite to this door. There's only two and a half metres from the place where I am to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And this door that we see open here, is that the entrance to your home?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this is the front door, the entrance door to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would ask that this photo be tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P10, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd ask, please, that that photograph be taken off the screen, and if we could see -- this will be tab 3, 65 ter number 609, the photograph with the ERN number 0501-6271.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rami Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there seems to be a technical problem on my side of the room, because I'm still seeing the former exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, do you recognise the two people shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Who is shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Rami Jusufi and Elivje Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what relation, if any, was Elivje to your son Rami?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: She was his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, can this photograph be also tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P11, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could we now show the witness 65 ter number 197, with an ERN number N001-4925.10. And this is the last tab, Your Honour, in the folder that you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, do you recognise what is shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: This photograph depicts the yard and the entrance gate to my yard and a car, a Golf make - Golf II make - which was on my name registered, but since I was ill, my son Rami was driving it and taking me for therapy. On the other side, you see a building, a feature that was under construction, but the construction material for building it was burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see, in this vehicle that we can see, what had happened to that vehicle; do you know?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: I will tell you now in more details what happened to the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just briefly, just a very brief answer, please.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Briefly, after my son was killed, the car was burnt down. So the car was burnt after my son was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was the car burned on the same day that your son died?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know who burned this car?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: The police, the police burnt it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, at this time I -- I must admit -- I have a request. Could this photograph, please, be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P12, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. At this time, I have no more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps before you sit: The first photograph you saw of your son, Mr. Jusufi, if you remember, lying on the carpet on the floor, do you know where that photograph was taken and when it was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That photograph was taken on the 13th at 10.00 in my daughter's house, which is in the same village, in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know who took the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The hodxa, the Muslim priest of our village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, of course, you rely, Mr. Saxon, on the statement that has been tendered as the evidence-in-chief of the witness, pursuant to Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour, in addition to what -- and in addition, obviously, to what the witness has told us today about these particular four --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Well, then, we come then to cross-examination. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There will be questions by Ms. Residovic to you, Mr. Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jusufi, I am Edina Residovic, together with my colleague, Guenal Mettraux. I am defending Mr. Ljube Boskoski. On behalf of my client, Mr. Boskoski, on my personal behalf and on behalf of Mr. Mettraux, I would like to state -- to give you my condolences and the understanding about the grieving of your son before. Mr. Jusufi, from your data, I understand that you also understand Bosnian language. I understand you all, so the language that I speak --

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, you don't even need to interpret. I can just listen to the lawyer. I understand her completely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Jusufi, everything that me and you are saying must be interpreted so His Honour and the colleagues in the courtroom will be able to understand what we are saying. I would therefore ask you, Mr. Jusufi, when I end with my question, to wait a while for the interpreters to interpret my question, and then you respond to it, so everyone in the courtroom will know what you are testifying. Did you understand me, Mr. Jusufi? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jusufi, that we have met last year in your house in Ljuboten; yes?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I thank you for that, Mr. Jusufi, because you were the only of the Ljuboten residents that wanted to talk to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, you are Albanian by ethnicity and a Muslim by faith?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A while ago to the question of the learned colleague, you said that your family -- your last name is pronounced differently in Albanian and differently in Macedonian; is it so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But there is a custom among the Albanians that -- whereby a family at some time could change its name; is it so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your family, Mr. Jusufi, used to be called "Rashiti," so it is possible today that some people call you with your old family last name; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, is it correct that the Muslim names are recognisable?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And those are of Turkish or Arabic origin; is it so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No. I am not, by origin, Turk or Arab. I'm Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But personal names of the Muslim nation frequently bear the personal name which is Turkish or Arabic; is that so? Muslim names are similar?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct, they're similar.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jusufi, when I came to your house and when I introduced myself, you understood also that I am coming from a Muslim family; right?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You recognised that by my name; right?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jusufi, that at that time you told me that you are puzzled that I'm yours -- that I'm coming from a Muslim family and I am defending your enemy; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that I responded to you, Mr. Jusufi, that I -- that I am defending Mr. Boskoski, that he's not the enemy, but a friend of the Albanians, that he grew up with them, and that the Court will be the one to decide whether he is or he is not responsible for what the indictment charges him for?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's part of our discussion?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that time you very pleasantly said that you will be speaking with me about the events?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The conversation took place in your living room?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were lying in one part of the sofa, and I was sitting on the sofa that is on a 90-degree angle from the place where you were sitting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that moment, present in your house were your wife, your sister-in-law, the wife of the deceased Rami -- your daughter-in-law, I apologise, and your -- your grandchildren; right?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Jusufi, that at one point your daughter-in-law stated that her husband, Rami, has told her that he has seen the police from the roof in Brace's house early in the morning? At that time, you interrupted her, you told her that she was not in the house, you told her that you have already given a statement to the Prosecutor, and that you do not want to change that statement. Do you remember that part of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: We didn't have such a conversation, but we interrupted it because these were rumours. I didn't say this. I said only that when the son returned in the evening, in the evening of Saturday, he said that, "I hardly made it because of the police." And maybe Boskoski was there, too, because I saw many policemen. That's why I interrupted her, because this is not correct, because he said "maybe," he didn't say that he was. So there is a difference between that, so that's why I interrupted her, because as I said, there is a difference. It is probable or maybe he was, but it's different if you say he was. That is the reason that I interrupted her, because it was simply on an unbased rumour, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You asked your daughter-in-law to leave the room, and after that there was only me and you having a conversation; was it so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jusufi, I would like to ask you some general questions so we could better understand the entire situation. Mr. Jusufi, since you were born, you've been living in Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ljuboten is placed at the slopes of Skopska Crna Mountain?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the village of Ljuboten, Skopje could be seen very well, so its position is practically -- this situation practically dominates over the Skopje valley; is it so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are -- do you know, Mr. Jusufi, that above the village there is -- there are Ljubotenski Bachilo, and then Bacula comes and then Crn Common [phoen]; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jusufi, that for ages in that area above the village of Ljuboten, there was a road that caravans used to pass by and people used to call me -- call it Sultana Vaxada [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: That was the road of Sultan Murat.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, that road was used to connect the southern parts of Serbia, the areas around Kumanovo, towards Tetovo and Kosovo; is it so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, the road was not that. That road was to be used by people walking or riding on horseback. It was a narrow path. You couldn't drive a car on that road. It was built during the Turkish time. Now we use another path, another road.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, maybe we misunderstood each other.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Okay. Well, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's exactly what I had in mind. During the Turkish time, the road was used to connect the East with the West?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: You are right, yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the disintegration of Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, so during the existence of the country, you are aware of that, that that road was frequently used as a road that was used by various smuggling groups, smugglers of fire-arms, of cigarettes, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Please stop here a little bit. That road does not go through Ljuboten. This road does not belong to Ljuboten. That road passes through Radisa, Brodec, Ramno. It is an asphalt road up to Tanushevc. The road you mentioned has got nothing to do with smuggling. That is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Bearing in mind this position of Skopje, especially during the conflict in the south of Serbia in the area of Kumanovo and Tetovo, could you agree with me that Ljuboten was of a very -- great strategic importance for Skopje?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, Ljuboten doesn't constitute any strategic point. We never thought that this would befall on Ljuboten. It had nothing to do with Lipkove or Tanushevc. It was a quiet -- it was another zone. Ljuboten was surrounded by Macedonians. The other village is situated in Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Skopska - correction - Crna Gora. That is your opinion and I respect it, but Skopska Crna Gora, where Ljuboten lives is, of course, of a great strategical importance for the -- for Skopje itself?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: They are strategic. Kucevishte is also a strategic point. There are 20 villages near Skopje. They are either 10 or 8 kilometres far from Skopje, and they're all linked to Skopje. Ljubans, Ljuboten, also is placed in a good strategic position, even better than Ljuboten. We are not here to talk about strategy here or strategic position.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but your village at one time used to be a subject of the distribution of the military forces of the Republic of Macedonia because they thought that that area is of a specific strategic importance?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, but we are Albanians, they are Macedonians. We are Albanian, and they thought that they should protect this village from someone entering it. That's why the army came there. But we didn't have anything to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that Ljuboten would not have anything to do with some attacks, and I could agree with you that at the time of the events in Ljuboten, it was not the focus of the attacks of the extremist Albanian groups, as was the case with Kumanovo or Tetovo, but could you agree with me that Ljuboten could serve as a significant logistics base for certain extremist groups from these regions?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, no. You must be sure that Ljuboten didn't even think of it and never thought to do that and never worked in that direction, not at all. I'm talking for the entire village of Ljuboten, because that is a village engaged in agriculture, hardworking village. It didn't have any interest, any stake in that, because if they did, they would have left the village like the others did, and they went to Skopje or to Kosovo. Ljuboten population remained there. We never thought and never dreamt of being in that situation when we were fired at.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Let me just ask you something else now.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the village of Ljuboten, that you could come from Skopje to the village of Ljuboten by the road leading through Ljubanci or the road leading through Radisani; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jusufi, that also an additional road was built that went around part of the village where the Macedonian population lives, and that you used to call that the Ljuboten road, Ljubotenski Pat in Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: That was a road that we built ourselves, because it was 3 kilometres far from the village and the entire population built it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. When you go from Skopje towards Ljuboten, from the direction of Ljubanci, the road passes by the house of Brace, which is located directly at the crossroad between the villages of Ljubanci and Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Brace is 100 metres away from my home. Brace's place was sold by me. He was my neighbour. I sold him that plot of land. He was a friend. My -- my son was a friend with him, too. He did what he did to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the house of Brace, you pass by several houses where Macedonians live, and then you come down to the crossroad at the bottom of which there is a shop; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That street is the main street in Ljuboten, and its name is Street number 5; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I don't know, I don't know the number, but you are right, that is the main road. I don't know its number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If one goes from that shop towards the Orthodox Church, the houses -- your house, the house of Kenan Jusufi, of Xhabir Jusufi and Sefer Jusufi were located; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, and more, some more houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Immediately adjacent to the shop, there is a narrow lane where there is a new house of your neighbour, Fatmir Kamberi, and his brother, Memshi Kamberi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Kamberi, Memshi.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, brother.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: He's not at the road there, it is 50 metres in the -- inside the road. You are talking about Fatmir?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A new house of Fatmir and a house of Meshir?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: I believe it was three new houses, yes. There are three such houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I was aware of the two only. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you would go from the shop towards the mosque that is located in the centre of the village, at the very road -- at the main road, the houses of Sabit Jusufi are located, as well as Xhevdet Jusufi, the old house of Fatmir Kamberi --

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- and across from the old house of Fatmir Kamberi, there is the house of the Macedonian Sande Kostovski?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: You have passed that house. Sabit Jusufi, Nazmi Jusufi, Xhevdet Jusufi, Agim Jusufi, Kamberi Fatmir and Sande Kostovski. It's above Sande's road, but I don't think you mentioned the houses in proper line as they are situated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, majority of the houses belong -- most of the houses belong to the Jusufi family?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Ten houses altogether, ten or twelve, I think. Jusufi or Rashit, that's the last name, but it's the same family.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that, Mr. Jusufi, is otherwise the way in which the Albanian families used to live, especially in villages. The family is related by blood, by the male stream, were normally living in the same neighbourhood; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, they live close together, 10, 20 metres far from one another, whatever comprises the Jusufi family.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And all those houses that were facing the main street, those that I have mentioned and the ones that you added because I failed to mention them, they were, as your house is, surrounded by a wall so that the family life is protected from the views and the curiosity of the passersby on the street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: All these houses have big gates that divide them from the street, so you can see 10 or 12 doors one after the other and they all belong to the Rashiti family or Jusufi otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to ask now that the witness is shown Prosecutor's number 65 ter 199.3. Yesterday that document was given Prosecutor's exhibit number P3.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, could you tell me whether you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. This is a photo of my own house. It's a courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you know if you have some instrument to point?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to give one to you.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: I can't reach the figure there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I don't think it will be visible. We will provide the witness with a hard-copy photograph, and I would like to ask you to put it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: It is irrelevant. I can see whatever you want me to see and I will say whatever I need to say. I will answer you in every question you'll ask me. Just ask me what you want me to say. You don't need to be discomforted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Jusufi, could you just use the photograph that you have, and show on the projector where is the main gate where you entered the house from?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Here. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jusufi, that behind that gate, the wall continues?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That we discussed before and which prevents someone from the street seeing what is going on inside the yard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. It's a little bit steep here and the wall isn't very high, and you can see, because I think it's one metre and 50 centimetres. You can see from this part. But from here [indicates], it's even more difficult, unless you see someone who is very tall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, could you point in the photograph where was your shed located?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: My shed is located -- it is not a shed. This here [indicates], you see the small gate, and after this there is a wall. And this is where the shed was, from this door to this door [indicates]. There were 10 cubic metres of timber and other materials, and everything was burned down. The gates, too, were burned down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jusufi, that from this main entrance your yard is on a slight incline towards your house?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. It's rather steep, like 10 degrees steepness. I can't be very precise. There is an incline.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Jusufi. Judge, maybe this is the right time to go into the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will need to break now for half an hour. Before we do, I would like to record in the transcript that when the witness was pointing to the location of his shed, it was to a position to the right of the camera which took the photograph, between the position of the camera and the fence and gate. And that is as we looked at Exhibit P2. We will adjourn now and resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We hope you are feeling a little better, Mr. Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I'll then ask Ms. Residovic to continue her questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, I would like to ask that the witness is shown again Prosecutor's Exhibit P2 that is on the ELMO in front of the witness, and now I would like to ask the usher to help the witness and provide him with a pencil. Mr. Jusufi, a while ago you have shown me the wall that continues from the gate onwards, so, please, could you note down the number 1 to indicate the part of the wall that is behind your house, towards the main street? Please write number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Here [indicates]? [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the witness has marked with the number 1 the wall that separates the yard of his house from the main street.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you, Mr. Jusufi, since before the break you have pointed also the corner where your shed was located with the wood -- with the logs that burned. Could you please write the number 2 there?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Here [indicates] yes. The wall near the shed, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has marked the direction where the shed with the logs was located.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, can one see in this photograph also the garden gate - kapidzik, the local name - through which you go to your garden?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by "garden." This here [indicates] is the yard, from the main gate up to this point here. This is the yard. And here [indicates] is the entrance to the house. You cannot call it yard. But this part here is the yard. From this point up to this point [indicates], there are 5 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. I would like to ask you, is that part separated by a door, by any garden gate, kapidzik?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, there is no garden gate here. This used to be open and has no importance whatsoever, no function.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you now to sign this photograph and write today's date, 8th of May, 2007.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Here? [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: 2007. And sign your name, please?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I now move that this photograph is admitted as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D1, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask now that the witness is shown P12. And considering that the witness could not write anything on the e-court, I would ask that the witness is assisted by the usher and presented with this picture, placed on the ELMO, that used to be Prosecutor's number 65 ter 197.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, this is a dual image. It depicts the same facility, so to say. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same image. There are no differences whatsoever between the two.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you only to mark the upper part of the image with an arrow pointing the way from the entrance door to the yard, to the gate, where it can be clearly seen also from this car what you have stated before, that your yard is on a slight incline, that there is a slope. So, please, make an arrow from the end of the car towards the bottom of the photograph. Yes, from there to the bottom part of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Shall I mark it with a line.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, a line. Just a line with an arrow?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. It's up to here. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have also stated, when I asked you what is the height of the wall -- I would like to ask you now to circle the man who is at the gate, and next to him write the number 1, since he is a benchmark for the wall that you can see?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: This is the main street. [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Next to the man?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, next to the man.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since the man is of a certain height, so please mark it with number 1?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: This wall is outside, not on my side of the gate.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there is some of yours as well?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: This is outside [indicates], while this one here is my wall [indicates]. This is on my side of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: And here is also on my side [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Then mark your wall with number 1?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: So my wall with number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mark the door, the gate, with the number 2?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: [Marks]. There's the gate number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And mark the man with the number 3?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Number 3. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you also to write today's date, 8th of May, 2000 --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then sign your name.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I am tendering this as an exhibit composed in the court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D2, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask now that the witness is shown 65 ter number 170, page 5, and we could also, with the assistance of the usher, show the witness and place on the ELMO a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, you are certainly able to recognise your house? This house, it is your house?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And on this paper, you again have two identical images; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they show the same image. They are completely identical. The entrance here on this one [indicates] and the entrance on the other one as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you, Mr. Jusufi, if you are able to point or to say whether this small black frame that can be seen on the left-hand side is the frame of the window to the living room.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Here [indicates], yes, it's the window to the room on the left. As you enter the house, the house -- the room on the left side. This is the meter here [indicates], and this is the mark that was hit by the police [indicates], and I have not changed it. I keep it that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you mark the frame with the number 1, so that we know that this is the window? Yes, precisely there.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Number 1. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have marked here the window frame of the living room window where you -- into which you enter when you enter the corridor and then on the left-hand side. Above that window, one could see upstairs the frame of another window. Could you tell me, what room does this window belong to?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: To the room on the upper floor. This is the ground floor [indicates], and this is the upper floor. We call it the second floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me whether that is a room that was customarily used by your son, Rami Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: He used two rooms; this one and this one here [indicates]. He had two rooms in the upper floor, and I had two rooms in the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you then mark the entire upper floor with the number 2, which confirms that your son Rami used the rooms on the floor, on the upper floor?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, Mr. Jusufi, whether during that time, 11th and 12th of August, your son Rami again used those rooms on the upper floor.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: On the 12th of August, you mean?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: It should be the 11th, and he did not use this room on the 11th of August. On the 11th, he slept here [indicates] in the room with me, because his wife was not there. The children were, but his wife was not. You should first ask me how it came to that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. "The children were not there."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Would you then write the date on this picture as well and sign your name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will sign the date, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, there's no need for you to do that. Thank you. I'm just saying, Ms. Residovic, because of the electronic technology we now use, there's really no need, in the course of this trial, for you to have a witness sign and date. Certainly have them mark 1, 2, 3, the different things you need, but we've got the whole image then captured, so it will speed things up if we don't date and sign the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. This is the first time for me that I participate in a trial that uses e-court, and thank you for reminding me of this fact. Thank you. You may now remove the photographs that were placed in front of the witness, and I tender this photograph marked by the witness and ask that it receives an exhibit number as an evidence constructed in the court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 23, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, you spoke earlier that there were no problems in the village of Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. In the past, we didn't have problems, but we, during this time, were not in peace. Personally, I was, in a way, but the children were very scared because of the shootings and because of the roadblocks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Jusufi, could you remember that as early as in 1992, there was a process in the course of which in 1994 some persons, such as Mithat Emini and Hasan Agushi, Hysen Haskaj, and others were convicted because they attempted, in the village of Ljuboten, to establish a paramilitary independent unit? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, no. I'm hearing about this for the first time today. At that time, I was employed, I was working in a state company, and I was not interested in these matters, and I never heard of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. With regards to the events that took place between the 10th and 12th of August, 2001, in which, unfortunately, your son lost his life, you, Mr. Jusufi, have discussed them very frequently not only with the Defence but also with the representatives of international organisations, journalists, and of course repeatedly with the investigators of the OTP of the ICTY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, we did talk to them and explained what happened to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask now that 65 ter number ID 24 is shown, page ID 0297. 1D. Maybe I misread. 65 ter number 1D, page 1D0297.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document, Mr. Jusufi, is in the English language, and I would like to ask you: Is it correct that you, in April of 2007, when this file started, made a statement to the journalists of the Associated Press so that in the report of the journalists of this agency, Karantin Kry [phoen], it is stated, I quote: "Jusufi expects the trip to The Hague to testify in the case despite the fact that he is paralysed. He says that he hopes to see Boskoski and Tarculovski convicted." Is it correct that you have stated this?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: I did not say "convicted." I did say that I'm ready to travel to The Hague, but it's not up to me whether they will be convicted or not. There's another body who has the duty to do that. I said that I was ready to travel to The Hague and testify before this Court, but I did not say that I want to see Tarculovski and Boskoski convicted. As I said, it's another organ who decides on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If these journalists have quoted you as I have stated, it is obvious then that they misinterpreted your statement; is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: I believe it is so, because I did not say "convicted." He did kill someone of my family, but as for him, personally, there is another body that decides whether he will be convicted or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you, Mr. Jusufi: Have you also discussed, in 2001, the issues with the representatives of Human Rights Watch?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with this representative, and I don't think I've spoken to this person. I cannot say "yes." Maybe it is true, but perhaps I have forgotten about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would then ask that the document 65 ter 1D22 is shown, page 1D0287, Macedonian 1D0291.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, this is the first page, and the page where your statement is elaborated. Since you said that you maybe do not remember, that maybe you have spoken and maybe not --

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't remember at all. They did not say to me that these were who they were. As for the others, I know them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this report, I will remind you, it is stated -- this is a statement that you have made on the 20th of August, 2001, as it is stated in the report itself, immediately after the events. It is stated the following: "At the moment when the attack started, they came to my house. My yard was full. There were about 20 of them there. They were all wearing uniforms, but not masks as well. They shelled the gate to the yard. My son went to close the front door. At the moment when he closed the door and returned back to the room, there was a big blast. They demolished the door by -- they blew up the door by a machine-gun."

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: This is a mistake, this is a total -- a complete mistake. I will tell you now how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Please wait a moment: "That was the moment when my son was hit on the side and in his stomach from the shootings. He fell there. It happened right in front of my eyes."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask that the English version of this section of the text is shown; that is, 1D0288. So this is 1D22, while the page is 1D0288. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you have tried to interrupt me, stating that this was not true; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: What you read in the beginning, that is not correct. It is correct that he was killed while at the gate, but it's not correct that he went outside and then came back in. I will tell you now how it happened. What you just read was -- is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if Human Rights Watch wrote what I have just read, you are saying that they did not relay correctly what has happened and what you have told them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Partially, it is correct, but there's a part that is incorrect. The part that describes how he was killed near the entrance door, that is correct, but the part that was saying that he left and then came back, that is not correct. As he was going to close the door, that's when he was killed, at the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Jusufi, that after this interview with you and with Muzafer Jusufi, the representatives of Human Rights Watch made, that on the 23rd of August they visited your house, made some photographs, and you had still not returned. You were still not returned to your house then?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Muzafer was in Skopje. We stayed in Skopje for more than a month, for about 45 days. I don't know who gave other statements. I have given my own statement. Muzafer did not come back to Ljuboten for five months. He stayed in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you are certain that you did not return for the following three or four weeks to your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Six weeks, six full weeks. Now, whether six weeks make 50 days or 45, that I don't know, but it's six weeks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And neither your wife, Zenep, had returned to the house?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, nobody.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask that the document number 65 ter 1D2, page 1D0012, is shown. And I'm asking you: Have you, Mr. Jusufi, after the events, discussed them with the journalists several times?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: I have spoken with journalists on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have in front of us the document of the London newspaper "Independent," and their journalist is Justin Huggler? In paragraph 4 of 6th of September, 2001, has written that you have stated the following: "On the 12th of August, the police entered Ljuboten. They surrounded 20 houses around ours. There was an old man inside the house." That means you, your wife, Zenep, and your son Rami and two relatives: "The relatives hid behind the shed while --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are not sure where the two relatives hid.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: " ... while Mrs. Jusufi hid behind the stove. We heard them entering into our yard. They shot into my car. Then they set it on fire. Then Rami remembered that the front gate was not closed and went to lock it. They shot him through the door."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I ask you the question, I would like to ask -- it is of use that I will have to learn about the e-court for several days. I ask that 1D0013 is shown. The next page, 1D2, page 1D0013. Yes. In the fourth paragraph is the part that I have just read to Mr. Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, Mr. Jusufi, whether the journalists of "Independent" have relayed correctly what you have stated to them then?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Meanwhile, the interpreters say it is the sofa where the relatives hid.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, this is not completely correct. There are things that are correct, but there are things that are incorrect. I will tell you the truth here today before these Honourable Judges, and what is in the report is not completely correct. They say that my son went out and came in, which is not true. I really don't know how to answer this question you're putting to me. My answer will be the same. When you ask me what happened, I will tell you exactly what happened. I have come here, passing thousands of kilometres in this state, to come and tell the truth. If I'm an invalid, that does not mean that my mind is not working properly. My mind is working properly. This report is not completely correct. There are things mixed up in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask now that the witness is also shown 65 ter number 1D25, page 1D0299.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the first page of the book IWPER, and I ask now that the next page is shown, 1D25, 1D0303, the last paragraph, and if you could show 1D0304, the first paragraph? Mr. Jusufi, as you stated that you have discussed frequently with the journalists and with the international organisations, this institute for reporting on war and peace has reported that on the 3rd of April, 2002, you have told them the following: "We've heard shootings. The power went out. My son jumped to close the front door, but the police was already inside the yard. They saw him and shot. He tried escaping, but he was hit and fell." You stated also that your son was shot by two bullets from his back, near his kidneys, that went through his stomach. He died an hour later. Have you stated this, Mr. Jusufi, on the 3rd of April, 2002?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please repeat the part from the moment "they entered the main door and until my son was killed."

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Is it written there, because there is a part which is correct in this report, but there are parts that are incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: "He tried to run away, but he was hit and fell." That is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
