utterances.text: This is wrong. That is a mistake, an absolute mistake. You must be sure of what I'm saying, Your Honours. I can tell you, if you want me, how it exactly happened, but this is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Jusufi, you are testifying that these persons, two from the Institute for Reporting on War and Peace, as well as the previous reporters, have incorrectly stated what you have said to them? Are you trying to say that?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: There are mistakes in it. Some things are correct. They said he wanted to leave, which is not correct. How could he go? He was sleeping. Where could he go?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, we will now go on to the statements that you have given to the investigators of the ICTY. You have already answered before that on several occasions you have talked to the investigators; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, we have.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I remind you, you have told the ICTY investigator and have given statements on 9th of February, 2003, then 3rd of October, 2003, then you have given an addition to the statement of February 9, 2003, and both these statements have been confirmed by the officer of the ICTY who came to Ljuboten; is it so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't know the date or how many times they came. This, I don't remember, but I do remember that they came. This I can say, I can confirm that they came and that I gave statements, but I can't give you accurate dates. What they have taken down, this is correct, but what you put to me earlier, this is not entirely correct. I do not fully agree with what you put to me. My son -- that you said to me my son wanted to leave, that they saw him and they killed him, this is not correct, this part is not correct. I think you must believe me, Your Honours, what I'm telling you, because if you don't believe me, neither God will believe me, because God teaches us to tell the truth, and God, Allah, has always said, "I love just men, the honest man." The fact is that my son -- the fact that my son left the house is not correct, and I don't want to lie here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise for the interruption, but there's a point that I feel needs to be clarified. In the translation to Ms. Residovic's last question, in the English translation, the last part of the question reads this way: "And both these statements have been confirmed by the officer of the ICTY who came to Ljuboten; is it so?" If that is an accurate translation, I'm wondering if Ms. Residovic could simply clarify what she means by "confirmed by an ICTY investigator," because it's unclear to the Prosecution, what that means.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would like to correct a mistake that I have made, which is that the statement of the 3rd of October had not been given in 2003 but in 2004, and in respect to the confirmation, I have said that the officer of the Registrar have certified this statement as -- as being a statement, and I now add 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, since, as I understood, there's no need to enumerate all the statements that you have given because you could not really remember the dates, I will feel free to show you each of those statements, and then you confirm whether you have given that statement and signed the same statement. I would now ask that the statement of the 9th of February is shown. It is 65 ter number 1D5, page 1D025, and the Albanian page 1D036.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Again, I apologise for the interruption. I simply would like to ask whether it is absolutely necessary to show these documents one by one to the witness to have him confirm that, yes, he signed them on a particular day. The consolidated Rule 92 ter statement that has already been admitted, at the beginning of that consolidated statement, refers to Mr. Jusufi's prior statements, and I'm just concerned about the health of the witness and how much extra time this will take to give his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. I see, Ms. Residovic, that it mentions the statements of the 9th of February, 2003, and the 3rd of October, 2004. Are there statements other than those that you want to have the witness identify?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would show all the statements that this witness has given, bearing in mind that -- about a very important fact, important for the defence of my client, there are large discrepancies. My esteemed colleague, Guenal Mettraux, have already noticed, and we will -- that settled with the OTP, and we think that the consolidated at least is not in line with what you, Your Honour, have said, so we were not able to use it in order to examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I gather from what you are saying that you want to identify with the witness certain discrepancies?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, is this your signature at this page?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: This one here? Yes. This one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now ask that the witness is shown 65 ter number 1D5, page 1D031, and in Albanian 1D042.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, you recognise your signature on this page as well; is it so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this statement that you have given, as well as in all the statements that you have -- that you were giving after being heard -- after being interviewed by the OTP investigator, you have said that the statement has been interpreted into you in the Albanian language, that it is true, and that is a result of your best knowledge about the event that has taken place. Have you said it in that way?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now ask that the witness is shown his statement of 3rd of October, 2004. That is 65 ter number 1D6, page 1D0052, Albanian page 1D0067.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this statement that you have given on the 3rd of October, 2004, your signature there?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jusufi, that every time, at the request of the investigator, you have signed all the pages of the statement that you have given?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. To the Tribunal, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now ask that the witness is shown the addendum to the statement of 9th of February, 2003. That is number 65 ter number 1D7, page 1D0091, and the Albanian page is 1D0095.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, is this statement of yours that you have given on the 11th of August, 2006, also signed personally by you?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Today, on the question of my learned colleague, confirms that you have signed also the consolidated statement, that you have signed on April 22, 2007; that is, P81, and the addendum to that statement, P82. Those are all the statements that you have given since 2001 to the investigators of the ICTY; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And each time, Mr. Jusufi, you have stated that everything stated in your statement is true, and that is to the best of your knowledge; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: It is true. Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask that the witness is shown 65 ter number 1D5, page 1D0028, Albanian page 1D0039.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement of 9th of February, 2003, you, Mr. Jusufi, have, as it could be thereby seen, stated that on Saturday, that is, paragraph 1, have seen five armoured cars, APC, and five covered trucks. You said that you were in your yard and that you have seen the vehicles going to the yard of the Orthodox Church. Have you said that?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, I didn't mention any numbers. I only stated that I saw some. That some might mean one, two, or three, but I didn't specify a certain number. This is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you to show the witness 65 ter number 1D10, page 1D0120, which is an addendum. And, correction, you have given to the Prosecutor on the 22nd of April, which have received the number P82 today.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 6, you have said, on the Saturday, at 2000 hours afternoon: "I've seen one APC and one covered truck." Now, Mr. Jusufi, you have said that you have seen several or some and that you never spoke of a number. Tell me, Mr. Jusufi, is it correct that all this statement -- all the statements about what you have seen, completely different?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, only the number. I have an issue with the number. But the fact is that I saw some, because at 8.00, 8.30, it was still light. You can see, and I was out in the yard at that time near the gate, and the gate of the church was open and I saw a convoy or police or soldiers. They were mixed. They were both.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But in -- there are facts in the statements that you have stated and signed about -- and all the facts are completely different. You must agree with me on that. Is it so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, no, they are not different. I am not changing anything here. I am saying that I saw them. This is how it was. There is nothing that I'm changing here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask now for you to be shown 65 ter 1D5, page 1D0028, paragraph 4. In the Albanian version, page 1D0039, paragraph 4. In this statement of 9th of February, 2003, you have stated that you did not sleep well that night and that you have awakened at around 6.00 in the morning. You have also said that your wife has assisted you to sit in your wheelchair. You have heard a noise of truck and Hermelins. You have said to your wife and to your son to remain in the house, and you have gotten out to see what was going on, and you have stayed there until 7.30?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask that the witness is shown number 65 ter number 1D10, page 1D0120, paragraphs 11 and 12. That is again number P8.2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the correction of the statement you have given on the 22nd of April, 2007, about this very fact, you have stated that you have awakened between 5.00 and 6.00 in the morning and that you have said only to your wife to remain in the house and that you will -- you were to see what was going on. Is it correct that these two statements differ about the fact -- about the fact when you have awakened and whom you have told to remain in the house?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: What you are putting to me about the time, whether it was 6.00 or 5.00 in the morning, I cannot confirm it to you that it was quarter to 6.00 or half past 5.00, but it was around that time, because usually I wake up at 4.00. I cannot sleep well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that specific day you are mentioning that "you didn't sleep all night," it was the 11th of the eighth month. At least this how I -- please explain to me.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Okay. Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to say that you have given different statements on 9th of February, 2003, and on 22nd of April, 2007, not only about the time but also about whom you have told to remain in the house. In the first one, you have said to the wife and the son and in the second you said only to the wife. Are these two statements different? That's what I'm asking you, whether they are different?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Jusufi, once you have gotten out in the yard, regardless whether it was in 5.00 or at 6.00, you have stayed in the yard until 7.30; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: That's true, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you were alone in the yard; right?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Myself and my wife woke up, went outside. Whether it was 5.30 or 6.00 in the morning, that I don't know. The fact is that we went out. She helped me a little bit. Then she went to do her things, her usual work. I stayed near the main gate. And while I was there, near the main gate, I saw that something was going on. I have something more to say. I realised then that something was going on. There was noise. I speak and understand Macedonian very well. I could hear conversations. Some were going in the direction of the church, some were going in the direction of the crossroads. There I heard a name --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Jusufi, I know that you told all of this to the -- in the statements that you gave to the OTP. I would like to briefly respond to the facts that I am about to point to you. Normally, if you have something to add to it, the Chamber will allow you to give additional explanations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mrs. Residovic, before you do, I'm sorry, but I think we should break now to allow the witness to have a further rest and because of the time, and we will resume at 10 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, before we adjourned, if you remember, you stated that in the morning, your wife took you to the yard, that she returned inside, and that you remained in the yard alone until you heard the noise, and that around 7.30 you went back into the house. I interpreted what you have stated, but I think that I did it correctly. Is that what you have stated?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: What you're saying now? Well, my wife did take me outside. She went back in, and I could hear their conversations because I understand Macedonian very well. To what I could hear, there were many of them. Many of them passed by. They were going in the direction of the church, maybe in the direction of the Brace house as well, but I heard many things said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Tell me just this: This is what I want to know. So your wife was not with you throughout the entire period of time in the yard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, no, she was nearby. She was doing her usual work. She was working in the garden, she was preparing the bread, baking the bread for the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask that the witness is shown 65 ter number 1D5, page 1D0028, paragraph 5. The Albanian page is 1D039, paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, in the statement made on the 2nd February 2003, you have stated that you returned into the house around 8.00, that you saw your son, who had woken up, and that he was still wearing his pyjamas.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask that the witness is shown 65 ter number 1D8, page 1D0101, and Macedonian page 1D0102.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The investigator of the ICTY, Arunkumar Balakrishnan, had an interview with you on the 12th of October, 2005, and then you told him that your son, who was wearing pyjamas and was asleep when the police arrived, you said that Rami came down to the door just because of the shootings that he heard. You have also stated that after your son died and was taken for the burial, you never changed his clothes. It was completely blood-stained.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to ask that the witness is shown number 65 ter number 1D10, page 1D0121, paragraph 17, that was admitted today as Prosecutor's Exhibit P8.2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, these are the corrections that you entered last month, 22nd of April, 2007, and then you stated, speaking about the clothes that your son was wearing, you have stated the following: "When I arrived into the house and heard the noise, and I thought that the door exploded, my son had woken up because of the noise. He was wearing pyjamas and he rapidly changed into his jeans." Do you agree with me, Mr. Jusufi, that these statements are different from one another?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No. What you said, that he came down, that is not correct. He was not upstairs. He was in the room on the ground floor. This is the sentence that is different. He did not come down. He was in the room on the ground floor. He was sleeping in that room, and he was wearing his pyjamas while he was sleeping. You said that he came down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, you have stated, haven't you, that your son was awokened [sic] by the blast. If I were to tell you that your wife stated on page of transcript 443, line 22 to 24, that she personally had woken your son up, would this differ again from what you are stating?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: No, it doesn't differ at all. We were there, both of us, my wife and myself, but the sentence you're reading is different. My wife and myself were in the corridor when the door exploded. My wife said to my son, "Wake up, son, because the door exploded." Both my wife and myself heard the explosion. This is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. In your statements to the Prosecutor of the ICTY, you have also spoken about the persons who were inside your house at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask that the witness is shown 65 ter number 11 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 1D5.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ... page 1D0028, paragraph 3, and Albanian page 1D0039, paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this statement that we have quoted many times, made on the 9th of February 2003, in the paragraph 3, you have stated: "I, my wife, and the older son, Rami, remained at home. Then two of our relatives came, Muzafer, Imret -- and Imret Jusufi, to have a breakfast with us."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask that the witness is shown number 65 ter number 1D6, page 1D0055, paragraph 15, and the Albanian page 1D0070, paragraph 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is your statement of 3rd of October, 2004. Then, Mr. Jusufi, you have stated: "Muzafer and his family, and I think the entire neighbourhood that hadn't left before the Sunday morning, simply ran when they noticed the police." And then in paragraph 19, you stated: "On the day of the event, the following persons were inside the house: I, my wife Zenep, Muzafer, the son of my uncle. The reason why we were still inside the house was that we could not run away anywhere any longer because I was in my wheelchair."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About the same facts, I would like that this statement number 65 ter number 1D8 is shown, page 1D0101, Macedonian page 1D0102.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of October, 2005, in an interview with the aforementioned investigator of the OTP of the ICTY, you have stated that: "During the night, no one was in the house." Muzafer Jusufi arrived at your house to have a breakfast and the morning coffee around 7.00 -- around 7.30. You have also stated that you made a mistake in your previous statement and that Imret Jusufi was not there inside your house on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: That's correct, only Muzafer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Later in your statement --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask that document number 65 ter 1D7, page 1D0092, is shown, and the Albanian page 1D0096.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is an addendum to the statement that you have given on the 11th of August about the events in 2003, you have stated that Muzafer Jusufi was inside your house when the police arrived. Then you have stated: "My wife, my older son Rami, myself remained in the house. On Sunday morning, two of my relatives came, not together but separately. Imret Jusufi came to our house around 7.00 in the morning. He brought me cigarettes and left immediately. Muzafer Jusufi came around 7.30, after we invited him to have a breakfast with us. He was inside our house when the police arrived. He hid behind the door during the entire time the police was inside our house."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding this same fact, I ask that the document 65 ter number 1D10 is shown, page 1D0120 -- 0020, paragraph 10. That is the Prosecutor's Exhibit P8.2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You indicated that Muzafer arrived on the Sunday around 7.00 to have a breakfast. You must notice, Mr. Jusufi, that your statements about the presence of persons inside your house are again different. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: It is not different. Only Muzafer was in the house. I don't see any difference. It must be a mistake. They both have the last name Jusufi. Only Muzafer was in the house. I have no reason to lie here. Even if there were two or three persons there, I would say there were two or three persons, but the truth is that I only had Muzafer in the house, and I had invited him to join us for breakfast. I told him, "Come, Muzafer, to have a coffee with us." He is an old man. This is a mistake, but I don't see it as a very big mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Jusufi, I will ask you now several questions about the death of your son.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask that the witness is shown document 65 ter 1D5, page 1D028, paragraph 6 and 7, and Albanian page 1D039 [sic], going to 1D0040.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement you gave on the 9th of February, 2003, you have stated that your son tried to close the door, but that all policemen shot at him. You stated that your son was hit in the stomach and he was bleeding heavily, and that you saw two bullet wounds on his body. You were beside him when that happened. Further, you stated that another policeman pushed the other wing of the entrance door, and he almost made the door fall onto you. The police officer said that they only had two persons in the house after he saw me in the wheelchair and my son, who was lying, bleeding heavily. "They did not see my wife and my relatives. I told them earlier to hide."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I would ask that the witness is, please, shown the document 65 ter number 1D6 in relation to this fact, page 1D0057, paragraph --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I speak now?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- paragraphs 33 to 35.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Am I not allowed to speak here now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are, but what is happening is that Ms. Residovic is quoting to you some statements and then asking you to indicate whether or not they are different from each other. And you are tending to answer that by saying, "Well, the truth of the matter is this," and that you had no reason to lie or that you made a mistake about some matter and so on. So that's what's happening, and if you feel of need to comment on a particular matter that is being quoted to you, you can do that. Understand that. But what is being quoted to you are previous statements that you have made to different people. I hope you understand what's occurring. If you wish to speak, you may.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? I just wanted to point out the facts about the time from the pyjamas up to the door. He was asleep. At that moment, his mother said to him, "Wake up, son." The door exploded. It was a very powerful explosion, as if they threw a bomb at it. They went to the door, at the entrance door. So he was in his pyjamas, but he changed into normal clothes within five seconds. That was very fast. He went to the door, entrance door, which was open, and they were there. They were firing in the air, and as soon as they saw him, because the door was wide open and he was trying to close it, they immediately shot at him, and he immediately fell down. This is the fact. I was there, myself, in the wheelchair, as I am today, and I am very calm now when I'm telling you about this. As for other rumours, whether it was like that or whether it was like this, that I don't know. I'm telling you what happened. But it is in your hands. You are the ones who will decide on this matter. I'm only here to tell you what the truth is. Now, whether he was at the door or further inside, that is too many details. What is a fact here is that he was killed at the entrance door. When the policemen came to the door and the door was this much open, he kicked it open, the policeman, and I saw this with my own eyes, and for a moment I thought that the door was going to fall on me. And the door touched the feet of my son, because my son fell on his stomach, and then I was just opposite to the policeman, and the policeman said to me -- he said in the Macedonian language for us to understand, "Here are only two people," and they turned their back. They didn't kill me. This is the truth. As for other things that you're asking me about, things that you're putting to me, you know best what to make of those things. You are the judges of the UN. This is the truth, as far as the killing of my son is concerned. So from the pyjamas until he changed his clothes, it was not more than ten seconds, and shortly after he went to the entrance door, and that's where they killed him. This is the truth. Now, whether it was like this or whether it was like that, again, it is in your hands to decide. I apologise. I'm ill. I can go on and speak with Ms. Residovic on this matter for hours and days, but what is important here is the act of killing and why he was killed. There was no reason for him to be killed. Excuse me for being this lengthy on this. That night, on Saturday the 11th, when he returned from Skopje, everybody was in panic, the women and children usually make panic, so I said to my daughter-in-law, "Take the children to my daughter's house," because that is in a little bit of like a valley, there was no risk. And then there was a suggestion for all of us to leave. But he had just returned from Skopje and he also said, "Well, what if they leave and then they are again sent back at the check-point?" I said to him, "Take the children, seven children, and go there to Rijeka, and we will remain in the house alone with your mother." And then he said to me, "Well, I cannot leave you alone here. "This is the truth, and nothing can change this truth. You are the honourable judges who will decide on this. This is what deserves to be analysed. As for other things, I don't know what to say. I really apologise for being lengthy and for taking so much time, but I'm very calm, believe me, I'm not nervous at all. I'm just ill, and I just want to get over and done with this testimony as soon as possible and leave. And please, Mrs. Residovic, I only know how I'm able to sit here, because I'm in this condition for years, and this condition has worsened 100 per cent as of 2001. I'm looking after four children with only 100 Euros per month. I have no other income. So please, Mrs. Residovic and all the of you here, relieve me of further questions. You are the ones who are leading the proceedings here, and, Your Honour, thank you for giving me the opportunity to speak on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What you've been saying is well heard and understood by us. Do understand, Mrs. Residovic is trying to see whether you can explain why you seem to have said some things that are different from what you now explain. So I think you should bear with her a little longer as she reminds you of some of the things in your earlier statements. You may be able to help her and us to understand why you have differed over certain matters. So carry on, please, Ms. Residovic, but do not lose --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- sight of the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with respect to your decision this morning, I will have to show some additional differences in the statements of Mr. Jusufi, and I assure you, Mr. Jusufi, that I understand that it is not easy for you at all. You must understand that the Court cannot reach a proper decision if I don't ask all the questions that I need to ask.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi --

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, you can ask me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A while ago -- I apologise. I just need to see. I was just showing you 65 ter number 1D6, page 1D057, paragraphs 33 and 35, and Albanian page 1D0072, paragraphs 33 and 35.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement of 3rd of October, 2003 -- 2004, you have stated that your son, after having been hit, he fell immediately, and falling down he closed the door. Soon, the door was opened. You have stated that the person who was there said that somebody was looking inside, and when he saw you and your wife, he stated that there were only two people inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I now ask that the document 65 ter number 1D7, page 190092 is shown, Albanian page 19 -- 1D0096.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is the correction that you entered on the 11th of August, 2006, when you again noted that the police officers did not see your wife and your relative. Do you agree with me that all these statements that I have shown you are different from one another, especially with regards to the moment when you saw the police officers, where you were, and whom have the police seen with you together? Do you agree that they're different from one another?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: I don't understand what you are putting to me. The police saw me or my wife? He didn't see my wife. The policeman saw only me. The policeman saw only myself, not my wife. When he kicked the door open, the door was ajar, and then I was facing him. It was then that he kicked the door. And when it was open, he said, "There are only two people here."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would ask --

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: My wife was inside. She was in the room.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would now ask that the witness is shown 65 ter number 608, page 7. If this photograph is not on the computer, I will ask for the assistance of the usher to display it on the ELMO. Okay, the photograph has appeared.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague, the Prosecutor, during the direct examination, asked you to recognise some photographs. Could you tell me if you could recognise your deceased son on this photograph, Rami?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, I can, Rami Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that this photograph is made in the house of your daughter, in the Durmishi mehalla?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That happened on August 13?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before your son was buried in the yard of your daughter?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Not in the yard. In -- in the garden.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the garden, okay. As far as I remember, you also said that these photographs were made by the local priest, the hoxha.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These photographs were given by you to the Prosecutor after you got them from your neighbour, Sulejman, called Suljo; is it so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Suljo?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sulejman.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: I forgot who brought them. I forgot it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, okay, never mind. Mr. Jusufi, the OTP investigator have shown you these photographs when he was in Ljuboten last month and when you gave the addendums and corrections to your previous statement; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This photograph was taken after your son was already dead; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now ask that the witness is shown 65 ter number 1D4, page 1D0021.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These photographs have been shown to your wife as well, and your wife - bearing in mind that this is about a photograph that was on the 65 ter list of the Prosecutor under the number 609, and it is number 0501-6265 - your wife said that, as it is stated here in a special sentence, after the picture was shown to the witness, she said that she recognises her son on the photograph, and she recognises his wounds. In the description of the photograph that you can see in column 2, it is said that this photograph is made before the death of Rami Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now ask that document 1D4 is shown, page 1D0124.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you already said, Mr. Jusufi, you were also shown these photographs last month?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D0124, 1D4, 1D-0124. I apologise. We have some mistake. Let's not dwell on this too much. We would ask for the assistance of the usher to show this document on the ELMO. I apologise. It seems to be the 1D10. 1D0021.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now we have the correct document on our screens, and under the number 608 we can see that the photo -- the photographs has been shown to you, and that you then said that you see this wounds, and you also said that he was put in that position, and that is he was put in that position by your mother and your relative in order to stop the bleeding. Did you say that, Mr. Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, "by the mother," not "by your mother."

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: Yes. His mother and Muzafer, who helped her. Mostly it was his mother. I didn't even see that. Couldn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But in the moment when these photographs were taken, in that position, you said that he was already dead, and those two statements must differ from one another. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: What do you mean, they differ? Can you repeat or highlight the difference for me, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your wife said that that photograph was taken while your son was still alive, and you, as it is written in the notes of the Prosecutor, said that the photograph shows the position in which your son was put by your wife and your relative in order to stop his bleeding. Today, you have said to His Honours that these photographs have been taken on the 13th in the house of your daughter when he was already dead.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: He wasn't photographed on the 11th, but on the 13th. On the 12th, in the evening, very late at night, we took the body to my daughter's house, and the next day the hoxha, the Muslim priest, came and took his photograph. The photo wasn't taken in our home. Maybe she didn't know that. She wasn't in her right mind when that happened. I don't know what she has said, but I know it very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, thank you. I would ask now that the witness is shown document 65 ter number 1D5, page 1D0028, paragraph 5, Albanian version page 1D0039, paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this statement of the 9th of February, 2003, you, Mr. Jusufi, said that among the police officers, you have recognised Dusan Kruskarov from Ljuboten. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI
utterances.text: That's correct, I recognise them by the voice.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now ask that document 65 ter number 1D18 is shown, page 1D0262 and 0263.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Ms. Residovic, we're going to have to deal with that tomorrow. We've reached 7.00, and in fairness to the witness and the need of the accused to be back in the detention centre, we must stop now. And we must ask you, sir, if you could return for the evidence to finish tomorrow afternoon. We will continue at 2.15. I think you'll find that much of the evidence is gone, so you shouldn't have to look forward to too great a time. Well, we adjourn now, and we resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 9th day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25
